content.title: How to watch Mariners games: Updated TV, streaming and channel info
content.text: Finally, an answer for local fans to the only real question surrounding the Seattle Mariners entering the 2026 season: Yes, you can watch them on TV. The Mariners on Wednesday afternoon announced programming updates on how to watch their games through traditional cable and satellite providers. Viewers with a Comcast/Xfinity subscription can watch M’s games on Channel 1261. Those who have a Charter/Spectrum subscription in the Seattle-Tacoma market can watch games on Channel 414. On Wednesday evening, the Mariners announced more broadcasting details. Notably, Mariners games will air on DirecTV on Channel 687. Viewers with a Charter/Spectrum subscription in Seattle-Tacoma, Yakima and parts of Oregon can watch games on Channel 414; Spokane viewers can watch on Channel 318 or 414; and in Montana on Channel 130. Games will also broadcast on Astound Broadband/Wave for viewers throughout western Washington, and on TDS in eastern Oregon and parts of Idaho. “These channels will appear soon if your package includes Mariners TV. We expect your package to include Mariners TV if it included Mariners Baseball last season,” the club said in a statement. The club says a full channel finder will be available Thursday morning at www.mariners.com/watch, ahead of the Mariners’ first game against the Cleveland Guardians on Thursday night. Last September, the Mariners announced they were shuttering ROOT Sports Northwest — their regional sports network responsible for airing the bulk of their 162-game schedule — and handing over their production and distribution rights to MLB. As part of that plan, the team created a new broadcasting wing, Mariners TV, and a new streaming service, Mariners.TV. People in Washington, Idaho, Oregon, Alaska, Montana or Hawaiʻi (plus British Columbia and Alberta, Canada) can stream Mariners games with no local blackouts on Mariners.TV. Plans are on sale for $99.99 for a full season or $19.99 per month. Those outside the Mariners’ territory can continue to stream games on MLB.TV.
